decisions.why: 405.2 states each object put on the stack goes on top of what's already there, which is the same last-in-first-out fact 117.7/608.1 supply for why Abdullah's Veil resolves first.
405.5 ('the top (last-added) spell or ability on the stack resolves') restates 608.1's resolution rule in the stack-zone section.
105.4 says a player asked to choose a color must choose one of the five colors and that 'colorless' is not a color, which is the answer stated even more directly than 105.1/105.2c.

608.2c's instruction to 'read the whole text and apply the rules of English to the text' is the CR hook for 'another' keeping its plain-English meaning, an alternative basis alongside the targeting rules.
101.3 ('any part of an instruction that's impossible to perform is ignored') states the same do-as-much-as-possible principle as 609.3 for Arcane Denial's failed counter clause.
202.3d covers the mana value of split cards and fused split spells; Hangarback Walker is not a split card, so the answer never uses it.
603.2 says the ability triggers automatically but 'doesn't do anything at this point', the same waiting-trigger fact 117.2a and 603.3 supply.

500.3 says the only steps in which no player receives priority are the untap step and certain cleanup steps, which is an alternative route to 504.2's 'the active player gets priority' in the draw step.
603.3d works by pointing at 601.2c-d for putting a trigger on the stack, so 601.2c is the same target-choice requirement stated in the casting section.
115.1 defines targets as the objects a spell identifies and declares as it goes on the stack, the same 'Flesh Duplicate never says target' point 115.10/115.10a make.
608.2n supplies the graveyard-bound event (an instant goes to its owner's graveyard as the final part of resolution) that Rest in Peace and Dauthi Voidwalker are competing to replace under 616.1.
704.3 states SBAs are checked whenever a player would get priority, which is the timing that lets 704.5g destroy the lethally damaged Voidwalker after the Bolt resolves.
117.5 restates the same SBA-before-priority sequence as 704.3 from the priority side.
117.3b ('the active player receives priority after a spell or ability resolves') is the other half of the same when-are-SBAs-checked statement.
305.6 defines the basic land types and their intrinsic mana abilities, the companion statement to 305.7's rule about setting a land's subtype to Mountain.
602.2 ('to activate an ability is to put it onto the stack and pay its costs') states the same stack-first sequence as 602.2a.
602.2b is what makes 601.2g/601.2h apply to activated abilities at all, stating the same mana-abilities-then-payment process for activation.
601.2a is the announce-and-move-to-the-stack step the judge explicitly names before the 601.2b choices, the same casting-announcement step.
702.56a defines replicate's trigger as copying the spell, the same 'the copies are copies, not casts' fact 707.10 supplies for dodging Chalice.
113.7a covers an ability outliving its source; nothing removes Stream of Thought's source here, so the answer doesn't rely on it.
608.2h is about an effect using current or last-known information; the copy count comes from replicate's paid cost, so this rule is never consulted.
607.1 defines linked abilities, the mechanism that keeps each Augury's 'cast a spell of each type from among them' tied to the cards that Augury itself exiled.
607.1c ('an ability that fulfills both criteria is linked to itself') is squarely the rule that makes each Aminatou's Augury track only its own exiled cards.
701.9a defines discarding as moving the card from hand to graveyard, i.e. the event whose destination Leyline replaces while the discard itself still happens and stays findable under 400.7j.
118.12 is the parent rule stating '[do something]. If [a player] does/doesn't' makes the action a cost paid on resolution, which is the same framing 118.12a gives the 'unless' wording.
508.1g is the optional-attack-cost step of the declare-attackers turn-based action, part of the same 508.1h-j sequence in which Propaganda's cost is chosen and paid.
506.1 lists beginning of combat and declare attackers as separate steps, which is what makes the mana from the earlier step empty before attackers are declared.
500.4 as written is about effects that last until a step expiring as it begins; the mana-emptying fact the answer needs is 106.4 (and 500.5), not this rule.
603.1 merely gives the [When/Whenever/At] form of a triggered ability; the answer turns entirely on the look-back-in-time exception in 603.10/603.10a.
613.1e names layer 5, where the judge's walkthrough starts ('In layer 5, Wayward Angel becomes black'), so it belongs with the other layer-assignment chunks.
613.3 ('then all other effects in timestamp order... dependency may alter the order') restates the within-layer ordering rule 613.7 supplies for layer 6.
205.1b covers effects that make an object an 'artifact creature' while retaining its prior types, which is how the animated Gateway is still a land after transforming.
611.1 defines the continuous effect that Karn's Touch creates on the permanent, the effect 712.18 keeps applying through the transform.
712.17 is about a double-faced card exiled face down remaining hidden; nothing here is exiled, so the answer doesn't depend on it.
614.6 ('if an event is replaced, it never happens') is the rule behind the judge's line that once one replacement applies the draw event no longer exists, part of the same 616.1 choice step.
614.7 states a replacement effect whose event never happens simply does nothing, the same point about the losing replacement effect.
612.10 says splice adds the spliced card's rules text and doesn't modify the spell's own text, the same limit 702.47a states in the keyword rule.
204.1 describes the color indicator as a printed symbol separate from rules text, the companion statement to 204.2's 'an object with a color indicator is each color denoted by it'.
704.6d is the state-based action letting a commander in exile go to the command zone, the same rule 903.9a states in the Commander section.
903.3 says commander designation is an attribute of the card that survives zone changes, and its example expressly covers a commander turned face down, which is the face-down half of the answer.
614.1c establishes that 'enters with' and 'as this enters' effects are replacement effects, which is what puts all four permanents' effects into the 616.1 ordering process.
115.1a states an instant/sorcery's targets are chosen as it's cast (pointing at 601.2c), the same casting-announcement step 601.2b covers for X.

118.9a ('only one alternative cost can be applied to any one spell') is the restriction spectacle is subject to under 702.137a, and it's why the answer has to check that Robber's permission isn't an alternative cost.
120.4b states damage is dealt as modified by replacement effects, which is the step where Obosh's 'instead' doubling (614.1a) applies to the three damage headed for Nevaeh.
120.4a covers excess damage being redirected to another permanent or player; Flame Spill divides damage by its own text, so no excess-damage rule is used.
613.3 ('then all other effects in timestamp order') states the same within-layer-6 ordering rule as 613.7/613.7b and even points at dependency.
712.8e says a transformed nonmodal DFC's mana value uses its front face and a copy of a back face has mana value 0, word for word the same content as 202.3b.
616.1 is the parent rule for choosing among competing replacement effects that 616.1a's self-replacement-first step belongs to.
614.8 gives regeneration's 'the next time it would be destroyed this turn, instead...' definition, the same shield 701.19a describes.
701.19b is the static-ability form of the same regeneration replacement effect definition.
704.5g is the lethal-damage state-based action the judge says won't happen until SBAs are checked, i.e. the SBA that 704.3's timing governs.
704.5 heads the list of state-based actions that 704.3 checks.
117.5 restates 704.3's rule that SBAs are performed each time a player would get priority.
117.2e says no player has priority while a spell is resolving, the flip side of 704.3's 'whenever a player would get priority' that keeps SBAs from running between Prismari Command's modes.
608.1 is the general resolution rule underlying 608.2c's 'follow the instructions in the order written' for the mode order.
106.6 is the parent rule stating mana-producing effects can create a delayed triggered ability that triggers when that mana is spent, which 106.6a then applies per mana.
614.1a establishes Mana Reflection's 'instead' as a replacement effect increasing the mana produced, the premise 106.6a operates on.
508.1a states an attacker must have haste or have been controlled continuously since the turn began, the same summoning-sickness requirement as 302.6.
726.4 is about the initiative passing when a player leaves the game and has nothing to do with restarting the game or summoning sickness.
118.8d says costs beyond the mana cost don't change a spell's mana cost and effects asking for that mana cost still see the original value, which is exactly the answer.
205.1a states that setting an object's subtypes replaces the existing subtypes of that set, the type-changing content of the layer-4 rule 613.1d that makes Tropical Island stop being a Forest.
406.3 states cards exiled face down can't be examined, the hidden-identity premise behind the manifest rules (701.40a/708.2) that make the question of telling the two permanents apart meaningful.
609.1 states a resolving ability creates effects, which is the judge's point that the discard being a cost under 118.12 doesn't stop it from also being an effect.
118.12 is the parent rule that 118.12a's 'unless' template belongs to, stating the [do something]/if-clause cost structure.
722.4 in this corpus reads 'in every zone, a preparation card has only its normal characteristics', which is about preparation cards and unrelated to what a controlling player can see (723.4).
614.1c establishes Rescuer Sphinx's 'enters with' / 'as this enters' text as a replacement effect, the same as-enters framing 614.12/614.12a rely on.
614.1a makes Primal Vigor's 'that many plus one instead' a replacement effect, the effect 614.16/616.1 then apply to the Sphinx's counter.
614.6 states the replaced counter-placement event is superseded by the modified event, the mechanics of applying Primal Vigor's doubling.
614.15 defines the self-replacement effect the judge identifies on Epicenter, which never gets to apply because 608.2b removes the spell first.
608.2c's 'read the whole text' instruction covers how Epicenter's threshold clause modifies its earlier text, the effect that never happens under 608.2b.
115.1a establishes Epicenter as a targeted sorcery whose target was chosen at cast time, the target 608.2b then finds illegal.

616.2 states a replacement effect can become applicable as a result of another one modifying the event, which is exactly why each new token's devour effect applies only after Anointed Procession's has been applied.
608.2d is the rule that a resolving ability's remaining choices are announced as the effect is applied, i.e. the on-resolution choice that 800.4g reassigns to another player.

305.7 supplies the answer's actual payload once dependency is resolved (setting a land's subtype to Mountain strips its old types and abilities and grants '{T}: Add {R}'), a fact no 613.8 chunk states.
509.1b is the restrictions half of the same declare-blockers legality check 509.1c states for requirements ('while not violating any restrictions').
726.2 is about the inherent triggered abilities of the initiative and has nothing to do with restarting the game or companion legality.
613.7d ('an object receives a timestamp at the time it enters a zone') supplies Wayward Angel's timestamp for the 613.7/613.7a comparison against Turn to Frog.
100.1a ('a two-player game is a game that begins with only two players') is the same begins-with test 800.1 states from the multiplayer side, and is exactly the judge's reasoning.
726.1 defines the initiative designation and is unrelated to restarting the game or the first-turn draw.

610.2 states that one-shot effects create delayed triggered abilities, which is the judge's basis for Virulent Wound's trigger not being a continuous effect and surviving into cleanup, alongside 603.7b.
100.1b ('a multiplayer game is a game that begins with more than two players') is the identical begins-with definition 800.1 gives.
100.1a's 'begins with only two players' definition is the complementary statement showing this game never became a two-player game when Blaine died.
614.6 states the modified event happens instead of the original, the replacement-effect mechanics behind Aven Mindcensor's partial search that 701.23f then says still counts as searching.

The answer's whole spine is that the threshold effect starts applying in layer 5 (color) before Turn to Frog strips abilities in layer 6, and 613.1e is the chunk that assigns color-changing effects to layer 5 - the same layer-assignment group the miner required on the near-identical question rg807.
613.1f names layer 6 for ability-adding and ability-removing effects, the alternative statement of the same layer assignment.
613.3 ('then all other effects in timestamp order') restates the within-layer ordering rule 613.7 supplies.
613.7b gives Turn to Frog's continuous effect its timestamp at resolution, the other side of the 613.7/613.7f timestamp comparison.

611.3c says characteristic-modifying continuous effects apply as the permanent enters and before checking what triggers, which is how Mycosynth Lattice makes the Aura an artifact in time for Panharmonicon's extra trigger under 603.2d.
400.7c states prevention effects applying to damage from a permanent spell continue to apply to the permanent that spell becomes, which is the answer stated directly.
729.2a is about supplementary decks moving to a subgame command zone; there is no subgame here, so the answer never uses it.

508.1 states declaring attackers is a single turn-based action whose listed steps happen in order, the same 'all attackers declared at once, checks before they become attacking creatures' point as 508.1a/508.1k.
508.1j is the pay-attack-costs step; neither Gaea's Liege nor Rhonas has a cost to attack, so the answer doesn't reach it.
508.1j covers paying attack costs, and there is no cost to attack in this Reverence scenario, so the answer doesn't depend on it.
614.1c establishes The Mimeoplasm's 'as this enters' text as a replacement effect, the same as-enters framing 614.12/614.12a state.
614.1b ('effects that use the word skip are replacement effects') is the same statement 614.10 makes about skipping being a replacement effect.

613.7a only backs the judge's parenthetical that Pristine Angel's static-ability timestamp doesn't change on untapping; the answer itself follows entirely from protection from each color being separate abilities.
